questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: Find the dimensions of $\frac{B}{\mu_0}$
questions.solution: $\oint B \cdot dl = \mu_0 i \Rightarrow \frac{B}{\mu_0} = \frac{i}{l} \equiv [AL^{-1}]$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: Solid sphere of mass $M$, radius $R$ exerts force $F$ on a point mass. Now a concentric spherical mass $\frac{M}{7}$ is removed. What is new force?
questions.solution: $F = \frac{GMm}{r^2}$, $F' = \frac{G(M - \frac{M}{7})m}{r^2} \Rightarrow F' = \frac{6}{7}F$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: Find out equivalent capacitance for the situation shown in figure.
options: $C_{eq} = \frac{A\epsilon_0}{d} \left(\frac{K_1 K_2 + K_2 K_3 + K_3 K_1}{K_1 + K_2}\right)$
$C_{eq} = \frac{A\epsilon_0}{d} \left(\frac{2K_1 K_2 + K_2 K_3 + K_3 K_1}{2(K_1 + K_2)}\right)$
$C_{eq} = \frac{A\epsilon_0}{d} \left(\frac{K_1 K_2 + K_2 K_3 + K_3 K_1}{2(K_1 + K_2)}\right)$
$C_{eq} = \frac{A\epsilon_0}{2d} \left(\frac{K_1 K_2 + K_2 K_3 + K_3 K_1}{K_1 + K_2}\right)$
questions.solution: $C_1 = \frac{2 \times A\epsilon_0 K_1}{2d} = \frac{A\epsilon_0 K_1}{d}$, $C_2 = \frac{A\epsilon_0 K_2}{d}$, $C_3 = \frac{A\epsilon_0 K_3}{2d}$. $C_1$ and $C_2$ are in series, giving $C' = \frac{A\epsilon_0 K_1 K_2}{d(K_1 + K_2)}$. Then $C_{eq} = C' + C_3 = \frac{A\epsilon_0}{d} \left(\frac{2K_1 K_2 + K_2 K_3 + K_3 K_1}{2(K_1 + K_2)}\right)$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: From a sphere of mass $M$ and radius $R$, a cavity of radius $\frac{R}{2}$ is created. Find the moment of inertia about an axis passing through the centre of sphere and cavity.
questions.solution: $I = \frac{2}{5} MR^2 - \frac{2}{5} \left(\frac{M}{8}\right) \left(\frac{R}{2}\right)^2 = \frac{31}{80} MR^2$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: Find the radius of curvature of the common surface of two bubbles ($R_1 > R_2$)
questions.solution: $P_1 - P_0 = \frac{4S}{R_1}$; $P_2 - P_0 = \frac{4S}{R_2}$. So, $P_2 - P_1 = \Delta P = \frac{4S}{R} = 4S\left[\frac{1}{R_2} - \frac{1}{R_1}\right] \Rightarrow R = \frac{R_1 R_2}{R_1 - R_2}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: From the given option, identify the diode connected in forward bias.
options: Diode p-side connected to Ground and n-side to -15 V
Diode p-side connected to 2 V and n-side to 4 V
Diode p-side connected to -10 V and n-side to 15 V
Diode p-side connected to -3 V and n-side to ground/higher potential
questions.solution: Only in option (1), the p-side is connected at higher potential (0 V) than the n-side (-15 V) of the diode.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: Radius of electron in ground state for hydrogen is $a_0$, then radius of electron in $\text{He}^+$ ion in $3^{\text{rd}}$ excited state is $a$. Then $\frac{a_0}{a}$ is
questions.solution: $r = \frac{n^2}{Z} r_0 \Rightarrow a_0 = \frac{1^2}{1} r_0$, $a = \frac{4^2}{2} r_0 = 8r_0 \Rightarrow \frac{a_0}{a} = \frac{1}{8}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: Ice at $-10^\circ\text{C}$ is to be converted into steam at $110^\circ\text{C}$. Mass of ice is $10^{-3}\text{ kg}$. What amount of heat is required?
questions.solution: $\Delta Q = \left(1 \times \frac{1}{2} \times 10\right) + (1 \times 80) + (1 \times 1 \times 100) + (1 \times 540) + \left(1 \times \frac{1}{2} \times 10\right) = 730\text{ cal}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A charge of value $q$ is placed at the edge of a imaginary cube of side $a$ as shown in figure. Find the net flux through the cube
questions.solution: Flux through 4 such cubes $= \frac{q}{\epsilon_0} \Rightarrow \phi_{\text{cube}} = \frac{q}{4\epsilon_0}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A closed organ pipe in $9^{\text{th}}$ harmonic resonates with $4^{\text{th}}$ harmonic of open organ pipe [$l_{\text{closed}} = 10\text{ cm}$]. Find length of open organ pipe.
questions.solution: $\frac{9v}{4L_c} = \frac{4v}{2L_0} \Rightarrow L_0 = \frac{8L_c}{9} = \frac{80}{9}\text{ cm}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: Now the battery is disconnected and dielectric slab of dielectric constant $K$ is inserted between the gaps of the plates. Now charge on capacitor is $Q_2$. Find $\frac{Q_1}{Q_2}$.
questions.solution: $\frac{Q_1}{Q_2} = 1$ (No further charge is supplied)

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: Which of the following graphs correctly represents the variation of resistivity ($\rho$) with temperature ($T$).
options: Graph showing non-linear increase of resistivity with temperature
Graph showing constant resistivity with temperature
Graph showing decreasing resistivity with temperature
Graph showing linear increase of resistivity with temperature
questions.solution: The resistivity of conductors increases with increase in temperature non-linearly.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: If whole YDSE apparatus is immersed in a liquid of refractive index $\mu$, then what is the effect on fringe width?
options: It may increase on one side and decrease on other side
questions.solution: $\Delta w = \frac{\lambda D}{d}$. For refractive index $\mu$, $\Delta w' = \frac{\lambda D}{\mu d}$, so fringe width decreases.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: Two spherical black bodies of radius $0.8\text{ m}$ and $0.2\text{ m}$ are at temperatures of $400\text{ K}$ and $800\text{ K}$ respectively. Find ratio of rate of heat loss.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: The equiconvex lens shown in figure is silvered on one side. For what distance of object from the lens is the image formed on the object itself?
questions.solution: $\frac{1}{F_{eq}} = \frac{1}{f_m} - \frac{2}{f_l} = \frac{-2}{R} - \frac{4(\mu-1)}{R} = \frac{-2(2\mu-1)}{R} \Rightarrow F = \frac{-R}{2(2\mu-1)}$. For object-image to coincide, distance should be $2f \Rightarrow |u| = 2|F| = \frac{R}{2\mu - 1}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: Light of wavelength $550\text{ nm}$ is incident on surfaces of cerium and lithium. Work functions are respectively $1.9\text{ eV}$ and $2.5\text{ eV}$. Then electron will be ejected from
questions.solution: $E(\text{eV}) = \frac{1240}{550} = 2.25\text{ eV}$. Since $2.25\text{ eV} > 1.9\text{ eV}$, electrons will be ejected from Cerium only.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: The figure shows an electron entering the space between the plates of a parallel plate capacitor with an initial velocity, $v_x = 10^6\text{ m/s}$ parallel to the plates. If the length of plates is $l = 10\text{ cm}$ and the electric field in the region $E = 9.1\text{ N/C}$, then the value of $v_y$ when the electron comes out of the plates is (Electronic mass = $9.1 \times 10^{-31}\text{ kg}$)
questions.solution: $t = \frac{l}{v_x}$, $a = \frac{eE}{m}$, $v_y = at = \frac{eE}{m} \cdot \frac{l}{v_x} = \frac{1.6 \times 10^{-19} \times 9.1 \times 10^{-2}}{9.1 \times 10^{-31} \times 10^6} = 1.6 \times 10^5\text{ m/s}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: Find the equivalent power of the thin lens combination shown in the figure, where $\mu_1 = 4/3$, $\mu_2 = 3/2$, and $\mu_3 = 4/3$.
questions.solution: Net power $= P_1 + P_2 + P_3 = \frac{\mu_1 - 1}{R_1} + (\mu_2 - 1)\left(\frac{1}{-R_1} + \frac{1}{-R_2}\right) + \frac{\mu_3 - 1}{R_2} = -\left(\frac{R_1 + R_2}{6R_1 R_2}\right)$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: The particle shown in figure is just able to complete the vertical circular motion. Find the ratio of kinetic energy at A to the kinetic energy at B.
questions.solution: $v = \sqrt{5gR}$. $KE_A = \frac{1}{2}mv^2 - mg\frac{R}{2} = 2mgR$. $KE_B = \frac{1}{2}mv^2 - mg\left(\frac{3R}{2}\right) = mgR$. $\frac{KE_A}{KE_B} = 2$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: The current drawn from battery in the circuit shown below is _____ A
questions.solution: $\frac{1}{R'} = \frac{1}{1} + \frac{1}{2} + 2 = \frac{5}{2} \Rightarrow R' = \frac{2}{5} \Omega$. $R = \frac{2}{5} + \frac{1}{2} = \frac{9}{10} \Omega$. $I = \frac{0.9 \times 10}{9} = 1\text{ A}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: For complex ion $[\text{NiCl}_4]^{2-}$ what is the charge on metal and shape of complex respectively?
questions.solution: $[\text{NiCl}_4]^{2-} \Rightarrow \text{Ni}^{2+} \rightarrow 3d^8$. $\text{Cl}^-$ ligand is weak field ligand and hybridisation is $sp^3$. Shape of complex is tetrahedral.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text:
Compare boiling point of given solutions
(i) $10^{-4}\text{ M NaCl}$
(ii) $10^{-3}\text{ M NaCl}$
(iii) $10^{-2}\text{ M NaCl}$
(iv) $10^{-4}\text{ M urea}$
questions.solution: $\Delta T_b \propto i \times m$. For urea $i = 1$, for $\text{NaCl } i = 2$. Boiling point order: III > II > I > IV.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: The correct decreasing order of electronegativity is
questions.solution: The correct order is F > Cl > Br > I.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Which of the following has maximum size out of $\text{Al}^{3+}$, $\text{Mg}^{2+}$, $\text{F}^-$, $\text{Na}^+$?
questions.solution: For isoelectronic species, more the negative charge more will be the size, also more the positive charge smaller will be the size. Ionic size order: $\text{Al}^{3+} < \text{Mg}^{2+} < \text{Na}^+ < \text{F}^-$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: The IUPAC name of given specie $\text{HOOC}-\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)-\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)-\text{COOCH}_3$ is
questions.solution: The correct IUPAC name is 3-methoxycarbonyl-2-methyl butanoic acid.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text:
Compare crystal field splitting energy ($\Delta$) for given complexes
(i) $[\text{Fe}(\text{CN})_6]^{4-}$
(ii) $[\text{Cu}(\text{NH}_3)_4]^{2+}$
(iii) $[\text{Fe}(\text{SCN})_6]^{4-}$
(iv) $[\text{Fe}(\text{en})_3]\text{Cl}_3$
questions.solution: Splitting energy $\propto$ Strength of ligand $\propto$ Charge of CA. Square planar $\Delta_{sp} > \Delta_o$. Order: II > I > IV > III.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Consider the given equilibrium reaction $\text{CO}_2(g) + \text{C}(s) \rightleftharpoons 2\text{CO}(g)$. If initial pressure of $\text{CO}_2$ is $0.6\text{ atm}$ and after equilibrium is established, total pressure is $0.8\text{ atm}$. Then, find $K_p$.
questions.solution: $P_t \text{ at equilibrium} = 0.8 = 0.6 + p \Rightarrow p = 0.2$. $K_p = \frac{(p_{\text{CO}})^2}{p_{\text{CO}_2}} = \frac{(2p)^2}{0.6 - p} = \frac{4 \times 0.04}{0.4} = 0.4$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text:
Statement-I: $\text{CH}_3 - \text{O} - \text{CH}_2 - \text{Cl}$ will show nucleophilic substitution by $S_N1$ mechanism in protic medium.
Statement-II: $\text{CH}_3 - \text{C}(\text{CH}_3)_2 - \text{CH}_2 - \text{Cl}$ will not undergo nucleophilic substitution via $S_N2$ mechanism easily.
options: Statement-I and statement-II both are correct
Statement-I and statement-II both are incorrect
Statement-I is correct but statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but statement-II is correct
questions.solution: $\text{CH}_3 - \text{O} - \overset{\oplus}{\text{C}}\text{H}_2$ is stabilised by resonance. Neopentyl chloride is sterically hindered for $S_N2$. Thus both statements are correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Which of the following acids is also known as vitamin C?
questions.solution: Ascorbic acid is also known as vitamin C.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: An electron of $\text{He}^+$ is present in $3^{\text{rd}}$ excited state. Find its de-Broglie wavelength.
questions.solution: $n\lambda = 2\pi r$. For $3^{\text{rd}}$ excited state, $n = 4$. $4\lambda = 2 \times \pi \times 0.529 \times \frac{16}{2} \text{ \AA} \Rightarrow \lambda = 6.64\text{ \AA}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Which of the following will show positive Fehling test?
questions.solution: Fehling test is given by aliphatic aldehydes except benzaldehyde. $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5-\text{CH}_2-\text{CHO}$ will give +ve Fehling test.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text:
$4f^7$ configuration is possible for
(a) $\text{Eu}^{3+}$, (b) $\text{Eu}^{2+}$, (c) $\text{Gd}^{3+}$, (d) $\text{Tb}^{3+}$, (e) $\text{Sm}^{2+}$
questions.solution: Electronic configuration of $\text{Eu}^{2+} \Rightarrow 4f^7$, $\text{Gd}^{3+} \Rightarrow 4f^7$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Given : $\text{NH}_2\text{COONH}_4(s) \rightleftharpoons 2\text{NH}_3(g) + \text{CO}_2(g)$. If the partial pressure of $\text{CO}_2$ gas at equilibrium is $0.4\text{ atm}$ and the total pressure is $1\text{ atm}$, then the value of $K_p$ at the same temperature is
questions.solution: Total pressure = $1.0\text{ atm}$, $p_{\text{CO}_2} = 0.4\text{ atm} \Rightarrow p_{\text{NH}_3} = 0.6\text{ atm}$. $K_p = (p_{\text{NH}_3})^2 (p_{\text{CO}_2}) = (0.6)^2(0.4) = 0.144\text{ atm}^3$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Identify the product in the reaction of 1-chloro-2-bromo-3-methylcyclopentane with excess $\text{NH}(\text{CH}_3)_2$.
options: Structure with Cl remaining and N(CH3)2 substituted
questions.solution: Bromide is a better leaving group, leading to nucleophilic substitution at that position followed by intramolecular/intermolecular substitution as shown in option (1).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: $\text{CO}_2$ gas is taken at $1\text{ atm}, 273\text{K}$. Now it is allowed to pass through $0.1\text{ M Ca(OH)}_2$ aq. solution. Excess amount of $\text{Ca(OH)}_2$ is neutralised with $40\text{ mL}$ of $0.1\text{ M HCl}$. Then find volume of $\text{Ca(OH)}_2$ initially taken if $50\%$ $\text{Ca(OH)}_2$ is react with $\text{CO}_2$
questions.solution: $\text{g meq of Ca(OH)}_2 = 2 \times \text{gm eq of HCl} \Rightarrow 0.1 \times \frac{V_{\text{mL}}}{1000} \times 2 = 2 \times 0.1 \times \frac{40}{1000} \times 1 \Rightarrow V_{\text{mL}} = 40\text{ mL}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: In a closed insulated container, a liquid is stirred with a paddle to increase the temperature, which of the following is true?
questions.solution: For closed insulated container, $q = 0$. From FLOT: $\Delta U = q + w \Rightarrow \Delta E = w \neq 0$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text:
Match the column and choose the correct option:
Column-I (Properties):
(A) Electronegativity
(B) Cationic size
(C) Metallic Character
(D) Electron affinity

Column-II (Order):
(1) B < C < N < O
(2) Li > Mg > Be
(3) K > Mg > Al
(4) Cl > F > Br > I
questions.solution: Electronegativity: B < C < N < O (1); Cationic size: Li+ > Mg2+ > Be2+ (2); Metallic character: K > Mg > Al (3); Electron affinity: Cl > F > Br > I (4).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Nitrobenzene $\xrightarrow{\text{Sn+HCl}} A \xrightarrow{\text{NaNO}_2 + \text{HCl}} B \xrightarrow{\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{OH}} C$. Identify C.
questions.solution: Nitrobenzene gives Aniline (A), which on diazotisation gives Benzene diazonium chloride (B). Reduction with ethanol gives Benzene (C).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Nitrobenzene $\xrightarrow{\text{(i) Sn/HCl, (ii) NaNO}_2/\text{HCl}(0-5^\circ\text{C}), \text{(iii) CuCl/HCl, (iv) Na/dry ether}} (A) \text{ (major)}$. Find molecular weight of (A) in $\text{g mol}^{-1}$.
questions.solution: The product (A) is Biphenyl ($\text{C}_{12}\text{H}_{10}$). Molecular weight $= 12 \times 12 + 10 = 154\text{ g mol}^{-1}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Calculate Number of stereoisomers of $\text{CH}_3 - \text{CH} = \text{CH} - \text{CH}(\text{OH}) - \text{CH}_3$
questions.solution: Number of stereocentres = 2 (1 double bond + 1 chiral carbon). Number of stereoisomers = $2^2 = 4$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: How many compounds have linear shape: $\text{SO}_2$, $\text{BeCl}_2$, $\text{N}_3^-$, $\text{I}_3^-$, $\text{NO}_2^+$, $\text{NO}_2$?
questions.solution: Linear shapes are: $\text{BeCl}_2$, $\text{N}_3^-$, $\text{I}_3^-$, $\text{NO}_2^+$. Total $= 4$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: In Carius method $180\text{ mg}$ of organic compound gives $143.5\text{ mg}$ of $\text{AgCl}$. Find the percentage of $\text{Cl}$ in the organic compound. (Nearest integer)
questions.solution: Mass of $\text{Cl} = \frac{143.5}{143.5} \times 35.5 = 35.5\text{ mg}$. Percentage of $\text{Cl} = \frac{35.5 \times 100}{180} = 19.72\% \approx 20\%$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Two ampere current is allowed to pass through molten $\text{AlCl}_3$ for $30\text{ min}$. Find the mass (in mg) of aluminium deposited at cathode. (Nearest integer)
questions.solution: Total charge $= 2 \times 30 \times 60 = 3600\text{ C}$. Number of Faradays $= \frac{3600}{96500} = \frac{36}{965}$. Mass of Al deposited $= \frac{36 \times 9}{965}\text{ g} = 335.75\text{ mg} \approx 336\text{ mg}$.

questions.solution: The partitions for a set with 3 elements are 5. Therefore, total possible equivalence relations $= 5$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: If $f(x) = 16(\sec^{-1} x)^2 + (\csc^{-1} x)^2$. Then the maximum and minimum value of $f(x)$ is
questions.solution: $f(x) = 17\left(\sec^{-1} x - \frac{\pi}{34}\right)^2 + \frac{4\pi^2}{17}$. $\text{Min} = \frac{4\pi^2}{17}$, $\text{Max if } \sec^{-1} x = \pi \Rightarrow 17\left(\pi - \frac{\pi}{34}\right)^2 + \frac{4\pi^2}{17} = \frac{1105\pi^2}{68}$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: If $8 = 3 + \frac{1}{4}(3+p) + \frac{1}{4^2}(3+p^2) + \dots \infty$ then the value of $p$ is
questions.solution: $8 = 3\left(1 + \frac{1}{4} + \frac{1}{4^2} + \dots\right) + \left(\frac{p}{4} + \frac{p^2}{4^2} + \dots\right) = 3\left(\frac{1}{1 - 1/4}\right) + \frac{p/4}{1 - p/4} = 4 + \frac{p}{4-p} \Rightarrow 4 = \frac{p}{4-p} \Rightarrow p = \frac{16}{5}$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: If $\frac{dx}{dy} + \frac{x}{y^2} = \frac{1}{y^3}$, $x(1) = 1$. Then $x\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)$ equals to
questions.solution: $\text{I.F.} = e^{-1/y}$. $x e^{-1/y} = \int e^{-1/y} \frac{1}{y^3} dy$. Putting $\frac{1}{y} = t$, $x = t + 1 - e^t e^{1-t} \Rightarrow$ for $y = 1/2$, $x = 3 - e$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: Let $T_r = \frac{(2r-1)(2r+1)(2r+3)(2r+5)}{64}$, then $\lim_{n \to \infty} \sum_{r=1}^n \frac{1}{T_r}$ is equal to
questions.solution: $\frac{1}{T_r} = \frac{4}{3} \left[\frac{1}{(r - 1/2)(r + 1/2)(r + 3/2)} - \frac{1}{(r + 1/2)(r + 3/2)(r + 5/2)}\right]$. Telescoping sum yields $\lim_{n \to \infty} \sum_{r=1}^n \frac{1}{T_r} = \frac{4}{3} \cdot \frac{8}{15} = \frac{32}{45}$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: If the images of the points $A(1, 3)$, $B(3, 1)$ and $C(2, 4)$ in the line $x + 2y = 4$ are $D, E$ and $F$ respectively, then the centroid of the triangle $DEF$ is
questions.solution: Centroid $G_1$ of $\Delta ABC = (2, 3)$. Centroid $G_2$ of $\Delta DEF$ is image of $G_1$ in $x + 2y = 4 \Rightarrow G_2 = \left(\frac{2}{5}, -\frac{1}{5}\right)$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: If $A = \{1, 2, 3, \dots, 10\}$, $B = \left\{\frac{m}{n}, m, n \in A \text{ and } m < n \text{ and } \gcd(m, n) = 1\right\}$. Then number of elements in set $B$ is
questions.solution: Counting proper irreducible fractions $m/n$ with $n \in \{1, \dots, 10\}$ and $m < n$: total distinct values $= 31$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: How many ways are there to pick 5 letters from English alphabets such that $M$ is the middle of the letters (repetition not allowed).
questions.solution: The middle position is fixed with $M$. We choose 4 letters from remaining 25 letters and arrange them in $4!$ ways: $^{25}C_4 \times 4!$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: Let a coin is tossed thrice. Let the random variable $x$ is tail follows head. Let the mean of $x$ is $\mu$ and variance is $\sigma^2$. Find $64 (\mu + \sigma^2)$.
questions.solution: Mean $\mu = \frac{1}{2}$, $\sigma^2 = \frac{1}{4}$. $64(\mu + \sigma^2) = 64\left(\frac{1}{2} + \frac{1}{4}\right) = 48$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: Let $g(x) = 3f\left(\frac{x}{3}\right) + f(3 - x) \quad \forall x \in (0, 3)$ and $f''(x) > 0 \quad \forall x \in (0, 3)$ then $g(x)$ decreases in interval $(0, \alpha)$, then $\alpha$ is
questions.solution: $g'(x) = f'\left(\frac{x}{3}\right) - f'(3-x) < 0 \Rightarrow \frac{x}{3} < 3 - x \Rightarrow x < \frac{9}{4} \Rightarrow \alpha = \frac{9}{4}$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: Let $\vec{b} = \lambda\hat{i} + 4\hat{k}$, $\lambda > 0$ and the projection vector of $\vec{b}$ on $\vec{a} = 2\hat{i} + 2\hat{j} - \hat{k}$ is $\vec{c}$. If $|\vec{a} + \vec{c}| = 7$, then the area of the parallelogram formed by vector $\vec{b}$ and $\vec{c}$ is (in square units)
questions.solution: $\vec{c} = \frac{2\lambda - 4}{6}\vec{a}$. $|\vec{a} + \vec{c}| = 7 \Rightarrow \lambda = 8$. $\vec{b} \times \vec{c} = 32 \Rightarrow$ Area $= 32$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: Let the parabola $y = x^2 + px - 3$ cuts the coordinate axes at $P, Q$ and $R$. A circle with centre $(-1, -1)$ passes through $P, Q$ and $R$, then the area of triangle $PQR$.
questions.solution: Circle passes through $(0, -3)$ and cuts x-axis at $(-3, 0)$ and $(1, 0)$. Area of $\Delta PQR = \frac{1}{2} \left| \begin{matrix} -3 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & -3 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 & 1 \end{matrix} \right| = \frac{3}{2}$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: If the circle $(x - 2\sqrt{3})^2 + y^2 = 12$ and parabola $y^2 = 2\sqrt{3}x$ intersects at $P, Q$ and $R$. Then the area of triangle $PQR$ is
questions.solution: Solving equations gives $x = 0, 2\sqrt{3}$. Points are $P(0, 0)$, $Q(2\sqrt{3}, 2\sqrt{3})$, $R(2\sqrt{3}, -2\sqrt{3})$. Area $= \frac{1}{2} \times (4\sqrt{3}) \times (2\sqrt{3}) = 12\text{ sq. units}$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: A hyperbola with foci $(1, 14)$ and $(1, -12)$ passes through the point $(1, 6)$. The length of the latus rectum of the hyperbola is

questions.solution: $\det(3 \text{ adj}(-6 \text{ adj}(3A))) = 3^3 (\det(\text{adj}(-6 \text{ adj}(3A)))) = 3^{21} \cdot 2^{10}$. Thus $n = 10, m = 21 \Rightarrow 4m + 2n = 4(21) + 2(10) = 104$.
